locale.pinyinConvention: Conventional lexical third-tone spelling; contextual 一/不 tone changes are shown. Pinyin is assistance, not a phonetic trace.

provenance.notes: Original alpha teaching material; structural validation is not linguistic or acoustic validation.

scenes.title: At the gate
scenes.objective: Introduce yourself and ask who someone is.
scenes.setup: A traveler arrives and meets a guide.

grammarNote.title: Identity and possession
grammarNote.body: Use 是 between a person and an identity. 我的朋友 means my friend; changing 我 to 你 changes whose friend is meant.

scenes.title: Looking for a friend
scenes.objective: Ask about a person and their location.
scenes.setup: The traveler asks for help on a village street.

grammarNote.title: Location and questions
grammarNote.body: 在这里 means be here. 吗 turns a statement into a yes/no question; 哪里 asks where. 不知道 means do not know.

scenes.title: At the bridge
scenes.setup: The journey reaches a small stone bridge.

grammarNote.title: Instructions and plans
grammarNote.body: 去找他 means go look for him. 别走 tells someone not to leave. 我在这里等你 identifies who waits, where, and for whom.

scenes.title: A clearer message
scenes.objective: Notice misunderstanding and ask for repetition.
scenes.setup: The guide and traveler clarify a message.

grammarNote.title: Understanding and repair
grammarNote.body: 听懂 combines hearing with the result of understanding. 没听懂 says that understanding did not happen. 请再说一遍 asks for another repetition.

scenes.title: The reunion
scenes.objective: Recognize an arrival and make a group suggestion.
scenes.setup: The journey brings the characters together again.

grammarNote.title: Arrival and suggestions
grammarNote.body: 他来了 announces an arrival here; 了 is not a general past-tense suffix. 我们一起走吧 proposes going together.

targets.en: be / am / is / are, in identity statements
he / him (same pronunciation as 她, she/her)
notes: Never use 他 versus 她 as an audio-only distinction without independent context.

targets.en: be at / in a location, in these examples

notes: Practice in whole sentences as well as this glossary entry. A neutral-tone particle is not a stand-alone content word.

targets.en: not present / not at the stated place
notes: 不 is pronounced bú before the fourth-tone 在 here; this is not a different negation word.

targets.en: go (to a place or to do something)
do not go / do not leave
okay / all right, in these replies
did not understand what was heard
has come / has arrived, in this scene
notes: This example presents an arrival/new situation. Do not teach 了 as a general past-tense suffix.

targets.en: let us go, in this scene

negation used in these location/knowledge statements
do not, used before an action
briefly / for a moment in this example
negates the completed/successful event in these examples
particle used for completed events or a changed situation, depending on the sentence
once / one more complete repetition here

utterances.en: I am going to look for him.

utterances.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ zài zhèlǐ děng nǐ.
utterances.en: Okay, I will wait for you here.
I will wait for him here.

utterances.pinyin: Xiànzài qǐng zài shuō yí biàn.

utterances.en: Let us wait for him together.

utterances.pinyin: Tā shì nǐ de péngyou ma?

utterances.en: Do not wait for me here.
We are going to look for him together.

utterances.pinyin: Tā tīngdǒng le, wǒ méi tīngdǒng.
Tā lái le, wǒmen zǒu ba.
utterances.en: He is here; let us go.

exercises.question: What does this person say?
exercises.explanation: 你好 is a greeting.

exercises.question: Who does this word refer to?
exercises.explanation: 我 refers to the person speaking.

exercises.question: Who does this word refer to?
exercises.explanation: 你 addresses the listener.

exercises.question: What is the speaker doing?
exercises.explanation: 我是… means I am…; Xiaolin is a name, not a word to memorize.

exercises.question: Who is being identified as Xiaolin?
exercises.explanation: 你是… means you are…; listen for 你 rather than 我.

exercises.question: What information is requested?
exercises.explanation: 你是谁 asks who you are.

exercises.question: Whose identity is requested?
exercises.explanation: 他 refers to a third person in this scene, not to I or you. Its sound alone does not distinguish 他 from 她.

exercises.question: How is that person related to the speaker?
exercises.explanation: 我的朋友 means my friend.

exercises.question: Whose friend does the speaker say they are?
exercises.explanation: 你的朋友 means your friend; the possessor has changed from 我 to 你.

exercises.question: What does this question word ask about?
exercises.explanation: 谁 asks who.

exercises.question: What is the question about?
exercises.explanation: 找 means look for; 谁 asks who.

exercises.question: What is the speaker doing?
exercises.explanation: 我找他 means I am looking for him.

exercises.question: Is this a statement or a question?

options.label: A question about whether he is here.
A statement that he is here.

exercises.explanation: 吗 turns this location statement into a yes/no question.

exercises.question: What does the speaker state?
exercises.explanation: 他在这里 states his location. There is no 吗 at the end.

exercises.question: Which location does this word indicate?
exercises.explanation: 这里 means here.

exercises.question: The question was whether the friend is here. What is the answer?

options.label: No, the friend is not here.
The speaker is introducing the friend.

exercises.explanation: 不在 answers that someone is not present at the place being discussed.

exercises.question: What information is requested?
exercises.explanation: 他在哪里 asks where he is.

exercises.question: Does the speaker know?

options.label: The speaker asks whether you know.
No, the speaker does not know.

exercises.explanation: 不知道 means do not know.

exercises.question: Whose location is requested?
exercises.explanation: 你在哪里 asks where you are.

exercises.question: What does this question word ask about?
exercises.explanation: 哪里 means where.

exercises.question: What is being asked?
exercises.explanation: 去 adds going to the question: 你去哪里?

exercises.question: What does the speaker intend to do?
exercises.explanation: 去找他 means go look for him.

exercises.question: What should you do in response?
exercises.explanation: 别走 is an instruction not to go or leave.

exercises.question: What information is requested?
exercises.explanation: 为什么 asks why.

exercises.question: Whose destination is requested?
exercises.explanation: 他去哪里 asks where he is going.

exercises.question: What should you do?
exercises.explanation: 等一下 asks you to wait a moment.

exercises.question: Who will wait for whom?

options.label: The speaker will look for someone else.
The speaker will wait for the listener.
The listener will wait for the speaker.

exercises.explanation: 我…等你 means I will wait for you.

exercises.question: Where will the speaker wait?
exercises.explanation: 在这里 explicitly identifies here as the waiting place.

exercises.question: Who is the speaker waiting for?
exercises.explanation: 等他 changes the person being waited for; compare 等你.

exercises.question: What does this reply mean here?
exercises.explanation: 好 can signal agreement in a reply.

exercises.question: What is being asked?
exercises.explanation: 听懂 means to understand what was heard.

exercises.question: What problem does the speaker report?
exercises.explanation: 没听懂 reports unsuccessful understanding, not refusal.

exercises.question: What instruction is the speaker repeating?
exercises.explanation: 我说 introduces what was said; 别走 is the repeated instruction.

exercises.question: Who did not understand?
exercises.explanation: 他没听懂 refers to a third person rather than 我, the speaker.

exercises.question: What does this chunk express?
exercises.explanation: 懂 gives the result of understanding to 听.

exercises.question: What does the speaker request?
exercises.explanation: 请再说一遍 is a request to repeat what was said.

exercises.question: Who should wait for whom?

options.label: The listener should wait for the speaker.
The speaker should wait for the listener.
Both should go find a friend.

exercises.explanation: 等我 means wait for me. The listener is being given the instruction.

exercises.question: What has changed?

options.label: The speaker no longer knows where to go.

exercises.explanation: 现在 means now, and 听懂了 signals the new understanding here.

exercises.question: What is requested now?
exercises.explanation: 现在 changes the time reference; 请再说一遍 still requests repetition.

exercises.question: What time does this word indicate?
exercises.explanation: 现在 means now.

exercises.question: What has happened?

options.label: He is still being searched for.

exercises.explanation: 他来了 announces his arrival in this scene.

exercises.question: What is the speaker asking for?
exercises.explanation: 在哪里 asks where; the subject is supplied by the conversation.

exercises.question: What location is indicated?
exercises.explanation: 在这里 indicates here.

exercises.question: Did the speaker see the friend?

options.label: No, the speaker did not see him.
The speaker asks if you saw him.

exercises.explanation: 我看见他了 reports seeing him.

exercises.question: Who has the speaker spotted?
exercises.explanation: 看见你 means see you; compare 看见他.

exercises.question: What is proposed?
exercises.explanation: 一起 means together; 走吧 proposes going.

exercises.question: What is the reply proposing?
exercises.explanation: 我们走吧 proposes that the group go.

exercises.question: What is the group invited to do together?
exercises.explanation: 一起等他 means wait for him together; do not answer from the scene ending alone.

exercises.question: Who does this pronoun refer to?
exercises.explanation: 我们 means we or us.

exercises.question: What does this word mean?
exercises.explanation: 一起 means together.

constructionExercises.question: Build this sentence: He is my friend.
constructionExercises.explanation: Start with the person, then 是, then the identity.

constructionExercises.question: Build this sentence: Is he here?
constructionExercises.explanation: The yes/no question particle 吗 comes at the end.

constructionExercises.question: Build this sentence: Okay, I will wait for you here.
constructionExercises.explanation: In this sentence the location comes before the waiting action.

constructionExercises.question: Build this sentence: Please say it again.
constructionExercises.explanation: 请 makes the request polite; 再 and 一遍 frame the repetition.

constructionExercises.question: Build this sentence: Let us go together.
constructionExercises.explanation: 我们 names the group; 一起 says together; 走吧 proposes going.

checkpointExercises.question: Whose friend is the speaker?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 他的朋友 means his friend; 我 identifies the speaker as that friend.

checkpointExercises.question: What is being asked?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 他是你的朋友吗 asks about his relationship to you.

checkpointExercises.question: Is he here?

options.label: The speaker is asking, not saying.

checkpointExercises.explanation: 不在这里 means not here.

checkpointExercises.question: Does the speaker know his location?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 知道 is positive here: I know. Compare 不知道.

checkpointExercises.question: What are you told not to do?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 别 negates the instruction 在这里等我: wait here for me.

checkpointExercises.question: What will the group do?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 我们一起去找他 combines we, together, go, and look for him.

checkpointExercises.question: What should you do?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 请 makes the familiar 等一下 request polite.

checkpointExercises.question: Did the speaker see him?

options.label: The speaker asks whether you saw him.

checkpointExercises.explanation: 没看见 negates seeing him; it is not the positive 看见…了.

checkpointExercises.question: Who understood?

options.label: The speaker did, but he did not.
He did, but the speaker did not.

checkpointExercises.explanation: The first clause is positive 听懂了; the second is negative 没听懂.

checkpointExercises.question: What is proposed after his arrival?
checkpointExercises.explanation: 他来了 announces arrival, then 我们走吧 proposes leaving.
